"import openpyxl

# Create the output workbook
wb = openpyxl.Workbook()
ws = wb.active
ws.title = "Sheet1"

# The VBA code that efficiently inserts 'Volkswagen' into column Q
# based on three conditions in columns A, B, and C
vba_code = '''Sub InsertVolkswagen()
    ' Efficient VBA solution using array-based operations
    ' Much faster than cell-by-cell processing for large sheets
    
    Dim ws As Worksheet
    Dim lastRow As Long
    Dim i As Long
    
    Application.ScreenUpdating = False
    Application.Calculation = xlCalculationManual
    
    Set ws = ThisWorkbook.Sheets("Sheet1")
    
    ' Find last row based on column A
    lastRow = ws.Cells(ws.Rows.Count, "A").End(xlUp).Row
    
    If lastRow < 2 Then Exit Sub
    
    ' Load columns A, B, C, and Q into memory arrays for speed
    Dim dataA As Variant, dataB As Variant, dataC As Variant, dataQ As Variant
    
    dataA = ws.Range("A2:A" & lastRow).Value
    dataB = ws.Range("B2:B" & lastRow).Value
    dataC = ws.Range("C2:C" & lastRow).Value
    dataQ = ws.Range("Q2:Q" & lastRow).Value
    
    ' Single pass through the in-memory arrays
    For i = 1 To UBound(dataA, 1)
        If dataA(i, 1) = "Government" And _
           dataB(i, 1) = "Germany" And _
           dataC(i, 1) = "Carretera" Then
            dataQ(i, 1) = "Volkswagen"
        End If
    Next i
    
    ' Write updated Q column back to sheet in one operation
    ws.Range("Q2:Q" & lastRow).Value = dataQ
    
    Application.Calculation = xlCalculationAutomatic
    Application.ScreenUpdating = True
    
    MsgBox "Done! Volkswagen inserted in " & lastRow & " rows processed.", _
           vbInformation
End Sub'''

# Write explanation and code into Sheet1 cells A1:Q701
ws["A1"] = "VBA SOLUTION - Insert 'Volkswagen' based on three conditions"
ws["A2"] = ""
ws["A3"] = "Conditions: Column A = 'Government', Column B = 'Germany', Column C = 'Carretera'"
ws["A4"] = "Action: Insert 'Volkswagen' into Column Q"
ws["A5"] = "Method: Array-based batch processing for high efficiency"
ws["A6"] = ""
ws["A7"] = "Why this is fast:"
ws["A8"] = "1. Reads entire columns A, B, C, Q into memory arrays (single read)"
ws["A9"] = "2. Loops through arrays in memory (very fast)"
ws["A10"] = "3. Writes the modified Q column back in one operation (single write)"
ws["A11"] = "4. Disables ScreenUpdating and Calculation during processing"
ws["A12"] = "5. No repeated cell access - all operations are batch-based"
ws["A13"] = ""
ws["A14"] = "VBA Code:"
ws["A15"] = ""

# Write the code starting at A16, spanning multiple cells
code_lines = vba_code.split('\n')
for idx, line in enumerate(code_lines):
    cell_row = 16 + idx
    if cell_row <= 701:
        ws.cell(row=cell_row, column=1, value=line)

# Save the workbook
wb.save("output.xlsx")
print("VBA solution written to output.xlsx")"
